Connection setup and operation recipes

Use current device evidence rather than a saved model, address, app list, or desired-state template. Commands below use an explicitly selected ANDROID_SERIAL; replace example paths and packages with the actual task target.

Prepare access

Install Android SDK Platform-Tools from the official Android distribution and ensure adb is on PATH. Python 3.9+ runs the inventory helper without third-party Python dependencies. For UI work, install uiautomator2 in a virtual environment, or use optional uv run --no-project --with uiautomator2 python .... Follow uiautomator2's upstream setup for the selected device and record a compatible version when needed.

On the phone, enable Developer options and USB debugging through its actual settings. Connect a data-capable USB cable, inspect adb devices -l, and complete any device-owned trust prompt within existing authorization. An unauthorized row is not usable access; offline is a transport problem. Do not change broader security settings just to bypass an installation or trust failure.

For supported wireless debugging, use the phone's current pairing page and adb pair HOST:PAIRING_PORT, then adb connect HOST:CONNECT_PORT. Pairing and connection ports can differ and change. adb mdns services helps discover current services. Compare physical identities using the helper's inventory before treating multiple transport aliases as different phones. A reported identity may be absent or insufficient: use task context and phone-side observation to resolve ambiguity before mutation.

Inspect and operate

python3 <skill>/scripts/android_inspect.py devices --timeout 20
python3 <skill>/scripts/android_inspect.py ui --serial "$ANDROID_SERIAL" --package com.android.settings --timeout 20
adb -s "$ANDROID_SERIAL" shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abi
adb -s "$ANDROID_SERIAL" shell dumpsys package com.example.app

The UI command needs uiautomator2 in the same Python environment. Each ADB request is bounded separately; inventory duration can grow with device count. The UI command bounds connection and hierarchy retrieval together in a child process. A timeout does not prove a phone-side action failed. The helper only inspects; it does not tap controls, install apps, or alter settings.

After transitions, wait for the intended activity/control with a finite deadline and refresh the hierarchy. Prefer semantic selectors and actual switch state. A Flutter input may expose only hint; focus the observed input before sending text and reopen the page to verify persistence. Handle secret input through the recipient's approved secret route without echoing values or retaining clipboard copies. Password labels and recognized token forms are masked, but ordinary labels and unknown secret formats remain private.

If another app's overlay blocks a control, inspect its geometry without reading unrelated content. Move or dismiss it only within scope, then restore temporary changes when appropriate. A screenshot may expose more private content than the filtered hierarchy; capture only what the task requires.

Temporary display settings

Before sustained UI work, record the current value:

adb -s "$ANDROID_SERIAL" shell settings get system screen_off_timeout
adb -s "$ANDROID_SERIAL" shell dumpsys power

Choose a supported setting that covers the session, read it back, and check effective power policy. Some devices accept a large millisecond value such as 2147483647 (about 24.9 days); this is finite, not a universal sleep-disable command. Device policy or app overrides can impose a smaller effective limit. Do not assume zero or minus one means unlimited. If a finite maximum cannot cover the work, report the actual limit and use supported awake behavior.

Keep the original value in task continuity, restore it after phone work ends, and verify both the setting and effective state. Restore absence by deleting a task-created setting rather than storing the text null. A pause during ongoing work is not restoration; context recovery must retain the original value.

Install and verify an app

Establish an official APK source, package, ABI/build, and signature compatibility. Inspect the installed package first, then use an authorized installer, for example:

adb -s "$ANDROID_SERIAL" install -r /actual/task/path/app.apk
adb -s "$ANDROID_SERIAL" shell dumpsys package com.example.app

Read package/version and verify real startup. Installation success alone does not prove login, network access, or background operation. Inspect a relevant VPN/firewall allowlist if the actual environment uses one, preserve its running state, and test a real app request. A configured update interval is not evidence that a scheduled update ran. Avoid competing update managers for one package unless their responsibilities are deliberately compatible.

Files and optional shell bridges

Use bounded listings at the actual task path. For transfer, adb -s SERIAL push and pull are usually clearer than typing a long shell command. Verify remote shell quoting; local argument arrays do not remove Android shell interpretation. Confirm resulting file size/content or the app's imported result as appropriate. Clean up only exact task-created temporary files.

Shizuku, rish, and Termux are optional, not dependencies of this package. Use them only when the actual operation needs their capabilities; obtain setup instructions and binaries from their official sources, verify service state, and preserve their real permission boundaries. Do not assume boot persistence, root access, a particular terminal build, or a preconfigured installer.
